newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end holiday IBIS trade firmer.
newsitem.headline: German shares end holiday IBIS trade firmer.

text.p: German shares ended IBIS computer dealings on Thursday, drawing strength from a firmer dollar and shrugging off the clash between the Bundesbank and Bonn over plans to revalue the country's gold.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects computer trade in the 30-share index, ended up 8.78 points at 3,635.38 points, or slightly down from the DAX's bourse close on Wednesday at 3,636.42.
Bourse trading was closed on Thursday due to a regional holiday but the IBIS computer system, which operates from 0630 GMT to 1530 GMT, was open for regular activity.

The IBIS DAX initially ignored news of the Bundesbank and Bonn entering open conflict on Wednesday as the central bank rejected Bonn's plans to revalue its assets and the government said it would go ahead regardless, traders said.
"The market is holding on rather well," said Birgit Bachmann at BHF Bank in Frankfurt. "I think the market has reacted so far relatively positively to the fight."
Bachmann said the Bundesbank showed "it was not willing to give up its historic stance and accept a weaker currency."
Traders also noted the share market has been resilient even when the dollar recently fell under 1.70 marks and shrugged off losses in German debt futures in London.
They instead pegged gains to the dollar rising about a pfennig on Thursday on safe-haven buying amid growing doubts about currency union.
"The German share market has shown that it can stand on its own legs," said one trader.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants to revalue the bank's gold and currency reserves to give a much-needed injection of cash to Bonn's public finances as it scrambles to cut back its deficits to make the grade for European monetary union.

But the Bundesbank warned on Wednesday that Bonn's scheme -- which calls for a special profit transfer to be made this year and next on the basis of the higher valuation of gold and currency reserves -- could undermine the euro from the start.
Among specific shares, chemical groups Bayer AG and Hoechst AG ended the day with gains and topped the trading volumes.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa was mostly steady after reporting higher traffic in April.
Sportswear maker Adidas AG slumped 6.25 marks to 183.75 marks after reaching a new record high on Wednesday at 191.50 marks on its outlook for record 1997 profit.
